title: Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING

This Memorandum of Understanding is recorded on this {date} at {place}.

BETWEEN

{party_1_name}, {party_1_description}, having address at {party_1_address}, (PAN/CIN: {party_1_id})
(hereinafter referred to as "PARTY A" / "{party_1_short_name}")

AND

{party_2_name}, {party_2_description}, having address at {party_2_address}, (PAN/CIN: {party_2_id})
(hereinafter referred to as "PARTY B" / "{party_2_short_name}")

(Each a "Party" and together the "Parties")

promptInstructions: Draft a MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU). An MOU is a PRE-CONTRACTUAL document recording mutual intent and key commercial terms during early-stage negotiations.

TERMINOLOGY:
   - MOU (Memorandum of Understanding): general pre-contractual; mostly non-binding except carve-outs.
   - LOI (Letter of Intent): similar to MOU; often unilateral by acquirer / customer.
   - Term Sheet: very brief; bullet-point commercial terms; almost always non-binding except confidentiality / exclusivity.
   - Heads of Agreement / Heads of Terms: synonymous with term sheet.
   - Memorandum of Agreement (MoA): tends to be more binding than MOU; closer to contract.
BINDING vs NON-BINDING — CRITICAL DRAFTING POINT:

(1) In Indian law (Indian Contract Act 1872, S.10), what constitutes a contract is offer + acceptance + consideration + free consent + capacity + lawful object. If MOU meets these, courts will hold it binding regardless of label. Cite Kollipara Sriramulu v. T. Aswatha Narayana AIR 1968 SC 1028; Trimex International FZE v. Vedanta Aluminium (2010) 3 SCC 1.

(2) Therefore, to keep MOU non-binding, language MUST be UNAMBIGUOUS:
   - 'This MOU is non-binding and is subject to and conditional upon the parties entering into a definitive agreement on terms mutually acceptable to both parties.'
   - 'No legally binding obligations shall arise from this MOU EXCEPT for the obligations expressly stated to be binding in [specified clauses].'
   - 'Neither party shall have any liability to the other for failure to enter into a definitive agreement.'

(3) HOWEVER, courts have held MOUs binding where:
   - Conduct of parties shows they treated it as binding (Suresh Kumar Wadhwa v. State of MP (2017) 16 SCC 757).
   - Terms are sufficiently certain and no further substantive negotiation needed.
   - Performance has commenced (e.g., transfer of money / assets).

(4) Common BINDING CARVE-OUTS in non-binding MOU:
   (a) Confidentiality — protects information exchanged during negotiation.
   (b) Exclusivity / Standstill — parties don't negotiate with others during MOU period.
   (c) Costs — each party bears own costs.
   (d) Governing law.
   (e) Dispute resolution (relating to enforcement of binding clauses).
   (f) Term of the MOU itself.
   (g) Notices.
STRUCTURE:
Para 1: Title 'MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING'.
Para 2: Parties identification.
Para 3: BACKGROUND / WHEREAS clauses (recitals) — context, prior discussions, mutual interest. Each recital with WHEREAS.

Para 4: SUBJECT MATTER — clear statement of what transaction / collaboration is being explored. Examples:
   (a) Business collaboration: 'Parties are exploring a collaboration whereby Party A shall provide [X services / technology] and Party B shall [provide market access / capital / distribution]...'
   (b) Investment: 'Party A (Investor) is exploring an equity investment of up to Rs. [amount] in Party B (Investee) on terms set out below...'
   (c) Acquisition: 'Party A is exploring acquisition of [shares / business / assets] of Party B...'
   (d) JV: 'Parties are exploring formation of a joint venture company for [purpose]...'
   (e) Pre-litigation settlement: 'Parties are recording their understanding for settlement of disputes pending in [case], subject to definitive settlement deed.'

Para 5: BINDING CHARACTER — UNAMBIGUOUS:
   (a) Non-binding default: 'This MOU is non-binding and reflects only the present intentions of the Parties. No legally binding obligations shall arise from this MOU except for the obligations expressly identified as BINDING in Clause [X] (Confidentiality), Clause [Y] (Exclusivity), Clause [Z] (Costs, Governing Law, Dispute Resolution). The Parties expressly intend that no legal rights or obligations are created in respect of the proposed transaction itself unless and until the Parties execute a Definitive Agreement.'

Para 6: KEY COMMERCIAL TERMS — set out as INDICATIVE / NON-BINDING:
   - Pricing / valuation methodology.
   - Structure (asset sale / share sale / new co formation).
   - Consideration mix (cash / stock / earnout).
   - Closing conditions.
   - Indemnity caps / baskets (indicative).
   - Lock-in / non-compete (indicative).

Para 7: CONDITIONS PRECEDENT (for definitive agreement):
   - Satisfactory due diligence (legal, financial, tax, commercial).
   - Receipt of all regulatory approvals (CCI / RBI / FDI / sectoral).
   - Internal approvals (board, shareholders).
   - Financing arrangements.
   - Receipt of consents and waivers from third parties (landlord, lender, key customer).
   - No material adverse change.
Para 8: DUE DILIGENCE — Right of parties to conduct DD; cooperation; access to documents, premises, personnel; reasonable time.
Para 9: DEFINITIVE AGREEMENT TIMELINE — Target date (e.g., 60-90 days from MOU); reasonable extension if DD requires; consequences of missing deadline (MOU terminates with surviving obligations).

Para 11: CONFIDENTIALITY — BINDING:
   - All information exchanged is confidential.
   - Use only for evaluating the proposed transaction.
   - Restricted disclosure to need-to-know personnel + advisors (bound by similar obligations).
   - Return / destruction on termination.
   - Exceptions: publicly available, independently developed, lawfully received from third party, required by law / regulator.
   - Survives MOU termination for [X] years (typically 2-5).
Para 12: COSTS — Each party bears its own costs (advisors, legal, accounting, DD) unless specifically agreed.

Para 13: NO PUBLICITY — No public announcement / press release / regulatory disclosure of MOU or proposed transaction without prior mutual consent in writing (except statutorily required disclosures).
Para 14: NO PARTNERSHIP / NO AGENCY — MOU does NOT create partnership, agency, joint venture, fiduciary relationship, or employer-employee relationship.
Para 15: NO REPRESENTATIONS — Each party makes representations only in the definitive agreement; representations / warranties / commercial terms in MOU are indicative only.
Para 16: ANTI-ASSIGNMENT — MOU not assignable without other party's consent.

Para 17: TERMINATION GROUNDS:
   (a) By mutual agreement.
   (b) By either party on [X] days' notice (if non-binding MOU).
   (c) Automatically on execution of definitive agreement.
   (d) Automatically on expiry of MOU term.
   (e) On material breach of binding clauses (e.g., confidentiality breach, exclusivity breach).
Para 18: SURVIVING OBLIGATIONS — confidentiality, governing law, dispute resolution, costs continue beyond termination.
Para 19: AMENDMENTS — Only in writing signed by both parties' authorised signatories.
Para 20: NOTICES — Manner of giving notices; addresses for service.
Para 21: GOVERNING LAW — BINDING: 'This MOU shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India.'

Para 22: DISPUTE RESOLUTION — BINDING:
   - Negotiation between senior management first.
   - If unresolved within 30 days, arbitration under Arbitration & Conciliation Act 1996 (sole / 3-member; institutional / ad-hoc; seat at [city]; English / Hindi language; rules of [institution]).
   - OR exclusive court jurisdiction at specified place.
Para 23: ENTIRE UNDERSTANDING — MOU supersedes prior oral / written communications on subject matter but does not itself create binding rights except as specified.
Para 24: COUNTERPARTS — May be executed in counterparts.
Execution by both parties (authorised signatories with seal for entities).

STAMP DUTY — MOU stamp duty:
   - Generally low (Rs.100 to Rs.500 fixed) treating as agreement under Article 5 of state stamp schedule.
   - HOWEVER, if MOU has binding commercial terms equivalent to contract (e.g., binding sale of property, binding investment) — Stamp Authority may scrutinise and demand higher duty.
   - Where MOU touches on transfer of immovable property and creates rights — may attract registration under S.17 Registration Act read with S.53A TPA (part performance).
Witnesses are OPTIONAL for MOU (no statutory requirement) but recommended for evidentiary value, especially where binding clauses important.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Definitions — agreement, contract, proposal, acceptance, consideration
What agreements are contracts — free consent, lawful consideration, lawful object, parties competent
Agreements void for uncertainty — guard against on commercial terms
Specific performance — applicable where binding contract; not applicable to non-binding MOU per se
Agreement / MOU stamp duty — typically Rs.100-500 in most states; verify state schedule
Arbitration agreement — included as binding clause in MOU
Referring parties to arbitration; appointment of arbitrators
Anti-competitive agreements — flag if MOU contains exclusivity / market sharing among competitors

filing_checklist: Stamp paper per state Article 5 (typically Rs.100-500; verify)
Identification of parties — PAN + Aadhaar (individuals) / CIN + MOA (companies)
Authorised Signatory PoA / Board Resolution (for entities)
MOU not generally required to be registered under Registration Act (no transfer of immovable property interest)
BUT where MOU includes binding sale of immovable property OR pre-payment + part performance — flag potential registration and S.53A TPA implications
Where MOU contains anti-competitive elements between competitors — flag CCI implications
Where MOU involves foreign party — FEMA / FDI / RBI compliance considerations
Where MOU has equity / share aspects of listed company — SEBI / stock exchange disclosure considerations
Internal approvals: Board / Investment Committee for material MOU; document approval trail
Confidentiality undertakings from advisors before sharing MOU contents
validation_rules: binding_clauses_list must not be empty (at minimum: confidentiality, governing law, dispute resolution)
conditions_precedent must not be empty (typically: DD, regulatory approvals, internal approvals)
if binding_or_non_binding == 'non_binding_except_specified_clauses' — explicit non-binding language required + identification of binding carve-outs
if exclusivity_period specified — exclusivity_period must include start date + duration + scope
